text: A country where you find almost every experience that you must have thought of at some point in your travel bucket list. On one side, mountains nestled above the clouds and the world's largest caves. And on the other, crystal-clear beaches. World-famous Vietnamese coffee, Asia's craziest nightlife, the world's longest cable car, or French-style cities, or the raw history of the Vietnam War; there is so much variety in this one country that every day feels like you've arrived in a new land. Welcome to Vietnam. Vietnam is an S-shaped country located in Southeast Asia that shares borders with China, Laos, and Cambodia. It stretches for about 1,650 km from North to South. That is why, in a single trip, you get to see cold mountains, tropical beaches , modern cities, and centuries-old culture, all of it. Hey guys, this is Shashank and welcome back to my channel . So let's start our Vietnam trip. Come with me. Now let's talk about the best time to visit. Vietnam's weather varies quite a bit between the North, Central, and South regions. Therefore, it is better to choose the season according to the destination. For North Vietnam, including Hanoi, Ha Long Bay, Ninh Binh, and Sapa, October to December is the best. For Central Vietnam, including Da Nang, Hoi An, and Hue, February to August is the best. For South Vietnam, including Ho Chi Minh City and Phu Quoc, November to April is the best. And if you want to cover the entire Vietnam, then the period between October and April is overall the most convenient and comfortable. During this period, exploring multiple regions in a single trip is comparatively easier. This trip has been planned through a company called Way For Travel. So, if you want their details, you can see them on the side of the screen, and I will also put them in the description below, and if you are looking for a trusted partner, you can consider them. So, first, let's talk about how to reach. Traveling to Vietnam from India is quite easy. From Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Ahmedabad. Direct flights to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh are available. There are three major international airports in Vietnam. Hanoi in the North, Da Nang in the Center, and Ho Chi Minh in the South. If you book flights two to three months in advance, return flights can be found for around 20,000 to 25,000. I booked my return flight for 22,000, which also included 15 kg of extra baggage. If you want to travel on a budget, VietJet Air is the most affordable option, and if budget is not an issue, Vietnam Airlines is the best option. If you want to know how you can find the cheapest flights, just type "flights" in the comments. Now let's talk about visa and travel insurance. It is mandatory for Indians to get an e-visa to travel to Vietnam, and the good thing is that the process is quite simple. Indian passport holders can apply for a single-entry or multiple-entry visa. Which can be valid for a maximum of 90 days. And keep in mind that visa-on-arrival is not available for Indians in Vietnam. Therefore, it is necessary to get an e-visa before the trip. You can apply for an e-visa online through the official Vietnam Immigration website. For the application, you mainly need to fill in passport details, a passport-sized photo, entry/exit dates, and some basic information. If you need any help related to the visa, please comment "visa". I will share a proper guide with you. Normally, the visa processing can take around three working days. But do not take the risk of waiting until the last moment. I would recommend that you apply for the visa at least two weeks before your trip. And one very important tip: apply for the visa only through the official government website. I will put the link to the official e-visa website in the description. After visa approval, definitely carry a printout with your passport because you might need it during immigration. Now let's talk about travel insurance. Travel insurance is not mandatory for Vietnam. But I personally would strongly recommend it. Usually, basic insurance costs around ₹ 300 to ₹ 800, which is very useful in unexpected situations like medical emergencies, baggage loss, flight-related issues, or trip cancellations. Now let's talk about SIM cards and money exchange because a little smart planning here can save you a lot of money. Vietnamese Dong is used for daily transactions in Vietnam. Before exchanging currency, definitely check the current exchange rate on the screen. If you prefer to carry cash, it is better to take USD. Instead of purchasing Vietnamese Dong directly from India, carry USD. Do not exchange all your money at the airport. Only exchange $ 50 so that you can manage a taxi, bus, or basic expenses from the airport to your hotel. Instead of exchanging money at just one shop in the city, compare rates at three or four places. Besides cash, you can also use forex cards, international debit or credit cards, or neo-cards. ATMs are easily available in tourist areas of Vietnam, and cards are also accepted at major restaurants, malls, and shopping centers. Still, keep some cash handy for emergencies. There are some UPI apps that you can use in Vietnam. Write "app" in the comments and I will share its name. Now let's talk about SIM cards. There is no need to buy a SIM card directly from the airport because prices can be higher. You can get a local SIM from a Viettel official store , pre-book via Klook to pick it up at the airport, or get an eSIM from Agoda. You will easily find a SIM online for 400 to 500 rupees. Now let's talk about stay options. In Vietnam, you can find stay options for every budget. Just try to book a hotel in the city center area so that sightseeing, cafes, and markets are easily accessible. Hostels are a very affordable option for budget travelers. Where you can get dorm beds for 500 to 800 rupees per day. If you prefer hotels, you can easily find clean and comfortable double occupancy rooms for 1500 to 3000 rupees per night . And if you need a little extra space or a kitchen, Airbnb is a good option. You can find fully furnished apartments for 2000 to 3000 per night. If you want a list of the best Airbnbs, comment " Airbnb". I will share the complete PDF. So let's start with our Day One. Most flights from India to Hanoi are late at night and land between 5:00 and 7:00 AM . After immigration and baggage, you should be out of the airport by around 8:00 AM. Freshen up at the airport, connect to the free Wi-Fi, and exchange around $ 50 into Dong for initial expenses. Do not take a SIM from the airport because prices here are three to four times higher. After dropping your luggage at the hotel, first head to St. Joseph's Cathedral, whose French-style architecture will give you a Euro-vibe feel. From there, walk to Hoan Kiem Lake and explore Ngoc Son Temple. After that, definitely try the famous egg coffee or coconut coffee at The Note Cafe. After lunch, check into your hotel and rest for two to three hours. Make sure to go watch a water puppet show in the evening. Where you can experience Vietnam's culture and traditions in an interesting way. Now let's talk about local transportation. In Vietnam, you get options like self-drive bikes, Grab cars like Ola/ Uber, Grab bikes like Rapido, and local buses. The most budget-friendly option is a self-drive scooter, which costs around 400 to 500 rupees per day. Local buses charge 40 to 50 rupees, or Grab bikes charge 100 to 150 rupees per trip . Grab taxis charge a bit more, but they fit the budget. If you are traveling with three to four people. Exploring Da Nang by scooter is quite easy and convenient. But there is a common confusion here. Is an Indian driving license valid in Vietnam? It is mandatory to obtain an International Driving Permit. Which is used along with your Indian driving license. Let's go and see how it goes. Hotel pickup generally happens between 7:00 AM and 8:00 AM. Ha Long Bay is a UNESCO World Heritage site. After an approximately 2 -hour drive from Hanoi, you reach Ha Long Bay. There are basically two cruise options here. One is a day cruise, and the other is a two-day, one-night cruise. On a day cruise, you get activities like lunch, kayaking, and cave exploration. The night cruise has almost the same activities. But the experience is a bit more relaxed and luxurious. Because you stay overnight on the cruise itself. However, the price of a night cruise is almost 3x more expensive than a day cruise. On a day cruise, you first explore the Sung Sot Cave. Where you get to see beautiful rock formations with colorful lights. After that, there will be a bamboo boat ride or kayaking, which is included, where you can enjoy limestone caves and amazing natural views up close. And then there is a stop at Ti Top Island. Where you can swim and also explore the island. After the cruise, you will return to Hanoi in the evening . You are dropped off at your hotel by 8:00 PM. After freshening up at the hotel, you can head out to explore Train Street. Now let's talk about language and local behavior. The official language of Vietnam is Vietnamese, and very few people know English. So, be sure to download Google Translate before your trip, as the locals 'behavior and communication style might be a bit different. So, avoid unnecessary arguments. Deal with things politely and just enjoy the trip . Keep day three for Ninh Binh. Now, day three is optional. If you want to go to Ninh Binh, you can. Otherwise, as an option, you can also fly to Da Nang. People also know Ninh Binh as the Ha Long Bay on land. This is a full-day tour. Departure from Hanoi to Ninh Binh will be in the morning. Here, you first get to experience the Tam Coc boat ride . Where local women row the boats with their feet. It is quite a unique experience. After this, you visit the Hoa Lu ancient capital and explore temples connected to Vietnam's ancient emperors. If you like adventure, climb the 500 steps of Mua Caves and enjoy the amazing panoramic view of Ninh Binh from the top. After completing the tour in the evening, you get dropped off at your hotel in Hanoi around 8:00 PM. After freshening up, you can explore Beer Street and do some shopping. Now let's talk about food options. If you are a non-vegetarian, then Vietnam is a food paradise for you. Here you will easily find seafood, chicken, pork, beef, mutton, and many local dishes, and that too on a very low budget. And if you prefer vegetarian or Jain food, then there is no need to worry at all. You can find Indian restaurants in every major city. Veg and Jain food options are available there. Indian food is a bit expensive. Like, for two people, you will have to spend around 1000 to 1500 rupees. If you are staying in an Airbnb, you can take basic cooking essentials from India and cook for yourself. Just pay extra attention to children in crowded areas and when crossing roads, and always wear life jackets during boat rides or any water activities. Now, for pregnant women, keep the itinerary a bit relaxed . Avoid unnecessary long travel and enjoy the trip by staying in each city for two to three days. Day five, Ba Na Hills. Dedicate the entire day to exploring Ba Na Hills. Where the most famous attraction is the Golden Bridge. Where you can see the mountain view between the giant hands. Try to take the 8:00 AM cable car because the crowd is comparatively less early in the morning and you can take comfortable photos and videos. Definitely carry a warm jacket because the weather on top of Ba Na Hills is much colder compared to Da Nang. After the Golden Bridge, explore the French Village and Fantasy Park. On Day Six, start your morning by visiting Lady Buddha, a famous attraction in Da Nang. From there, you get a beautiful view of the sea and the city. After lunch, Hoi An is just a 45- minute drive from Da Nang. You can also easily reach there by renting a scooter for around ₹ 400. Hoi An is a beautiful ancient town. The yellow buildings and colorful lanterns make the entire town look very vibrant. First, enjoy a coconut boat ride in Cam Thanh Village and experience the traditional Vietnamese boat dance, then explore the Japanese Covered Bridge and the local market where you can also buy souvenirs. And as evening falls, make sure to take a lantern boat ride on the Thu Bon River. At night, the entire Hoi An town looks so beautiful with colorful lanterns that this experience simply cannot be missed. Now, let's talk about shopping options. There are plenty of shopping options available for both men and women in Vietnam, and prices are quite affordable. There are many international brand factories here , so you can find branded products and apparel for very cheap. Just make sure to bargain, as shopkeepers will initially quote you three to four times the price. If you need any help related to shopping, comment "shopping". I will share the complete PDF. After that , head out to the Saigon Central Post Office for sightseeing. If you want to cover maximum places in less time, the Hop-on Hop-off bus is the best option, covering the city's major attractions in about two hours. After this, visit the War Remnants Museum, where you will get a chance to understand the history of the Vietnam War and its impact. In the evening, sit at a rooftop café to enjoy the beautiful skyline and sunset of Ho Chi Minh City. Now, let's talk about important apps. Where along with a boat ride, you get a chance to explore traditional villages, coconut factories, and rice paper workshops. In the evening, return to Ho Chi Minh City, rest for a while, and then head to the airport for your return flight. Now, let's talk about drone rules.
